stem: Which of these is **capital expenditure** for a printing business?

options.rationale: Correct: a non-current asset that will be used for several years.

options.content: Buying paper and ink to use in printing jobs
options.rationale: Materials used up in the year are revenue expenditure.
A running cost: revenue expenditure.
A repair keeps the building as it was: revenue expenditure.

explanation: Capital expenditure buys, brings into use or improves non-current assets.

options.rationale: Correct: maintenance keeps the van in its existing condition.
Buying a non-current asset is capital expenditure.
An extension improves the premises: capital.

options.content: Legal fees on buying a shop
options.rationale: Costs of acquiring premises are part of their cost: capital.

explanation: Revenue expenditure covers running costs and maintenance; it benefits only the current period.

stem: Tendai pays US\$600 to install a new freezer in his butchery. How should the installation cost be treated?

options.content: Charged as an expense in the income statement
options.rationale: Costs of bringing an asset into use are capital.
Installation costs have nothing to do with sales.
The freezer is for the business, not the owner personally.

options.content: Added to the cost of the freezer as capital expenditure
options.rationale: Correct: installation is needed to bring the freezer into use.

explanation: The cost of a non-current asset includes everything needed to get it ready for use: price, delivery, installation and testing.

stem: Where is revenue expenditure shown in the financial statements?

options.content: As a non-current asset in the statement of financial position
options.rationale: Only capital expenditure is shown as a non-current asset.
Expenditure that has been paid is not a liability.

options.content: In the income statement (statement of profit or loss)
options.rationale: Correct: it is charged against this year's income.
Only drawings and losses reduce capital directly.

explanation: Revenue expenditure is an expense (or part of cost of sales) in the income statement.

stem: Which of these is a **capital receipt**?

options.rationale: Sales are revenue receipts.
Rent received is income: a revenue receipt.
Correct: it is borrowed money, not income, and must be repaid.
Commission is income from normal activities: a revenue receipt.

explanation: Capital receipts include loans received, capital introduced and proceeds from selling non-current assets. They affect the statement of financial position, not profit.

stem: Nyasha owns a guest house in Victoria Falls. Which payment is **capital** expenditure?

options.rationale: Repainting maintains the building.
Replacing worn parts restores the roof; it does not improve it.
Insurance is a running cost.

options.content: Adding two extra bedrooms to the building
options.rationale: Correct: the extension increases the earning capacity of the premises.

explanation: Improvements (extensions, upgrades) are capital; maintenance and running costs are revenue.
hints: Does the spending improve the asset or keep it as it was?

stem: A mechanic employed by Farai's transport business spends a week fitting a new engine that extends the life of a lorry by five years. His wages for that week are US\$350. How are the wages treated?

options.rationale: Wages for improving an asset are part of the capital cost.

options.content: As capital expenditure on the lorry
options.rationale: Correct: the work improves the lorry and extends its life.
A new engine that extends the life is an improvement, not a repair.
The mechanic is an employee; the work is for the business.

explanation: Spending is classified by its purpose. Wages to improve or install a non-current asset are capital expenditure.
hints: Classify by what the work achieved, not by the type of payment.

stem: Where is **commission received** shown in the financial statements?

options.rationale: Commission does not have to be repaid.

options.content: Added to gross profit in the statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Correct: a revenue receipt is income.

options.content: Added to capital in the statement of financial position
options.rationale: Income reaches capital only through the profit for the year.

options.content: Deducted from expenses as a capital receipt
options.rationale: Commission is a revenue receipt, shown as income.

explanation: Revenue receipts such as commission, rent and interest received are other income in the statement of profit or loss.
hints: Is commission part of the normal earnings of the business?

stem: Capital expenditure benefits the business for more than one accounting period.
explanation: True. That is why it is shown as a non-current asset and spread over its life through depreciation.

stem: The cost of repairing a delivery van after a minor accident is capital expenditure.
explanation: False. Repairs restore the van to its existing condition, so they are revenue expenditure.

stem: Chipo runs a hardware shop in Mutare. Classify each item.

left.content: Installing burglar bars on the shop for the first time

explanation: Buying an asset, its delivery and a lasting improvement (first-time burglar bars) are capital; fuel and wages are running costs.

stem: Classify each receipt of Rudo's business.

left.content: Proceeds from selling an old van
Interest received on a savings account

explanation: Loans, capital introduced and sale proceeds of non-current assets are capital receipts; sales, rent and interest are revenue receipts.
hints: Revenue receipts come from normal business activities; capital receipts do not.

stem: Sipho bought a grinding mill for his business in Gokwe. He paid: price US\$16,800; carriage to the site US\$540; installation US\$1,260; test run US\$300; lubricating oil for the first month US\$85; insurance for the first year US\$720. Calculate the amount to be capitalised as the cost of the mill.
explanation: Capital: $16,800 + 540 + 1,260 + 300 = 18,900$, so US\$18,900. Oil (85) and insurance (720) are running costs. Including everything gives US\$19,705.
workedSolution: 1. Capital: $16,800 + 540 + 1,260 + 300 = 18,900$, so US\$18,900. Oil (85) and insurance (720) are running costs. Including everything gives US\$19,705.
hints: Include every cost needed to get the mill ready for use.

stem:
Thandeka's payments during the year included:

| Payment | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Replacing broken roof sheets on the storeroom | 1,250 |
| Extension to the shop | 9,500 |
| Painting the extension when built | 640 |
| Repainting the old shop front | 410 |
| Security guard's wages | 2,400 |

Calculate the total **revenue** expenditure.
explanation: Revenue: roof sheets 1,250 (restore, do not improve) + repainting 410 + wages 2,400 = 4,060. The extension and the painting needed to complete it (9,500 + 640) are capital. Counting the first coat of paint as revenue gives US\$4,700.
workedSolution: 1. Revenue: roof sheets 1,250 (restore, do not improve) + repainting 410 + wages 2,400 = 4,060. The extension and the painting needed to complete it (9,500 + 640) are capital. Counting the first coat of paint as revenue gives US\$4,700.
hints: Replacing like with like is maintenance.
Finishing a new extension is part of its cost.

stem: Distinguish between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure, giving **one** example of each for a bakery.

points.description: Capital: buying/improving non-current assets with benefit over more than one year, e.g. an oven or delivery van
Revenue: day-to-day running costs or maintenance used up in the year, e.g. flour, electricity, wages, oven repairs

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Capital expenditure buys or improves long-term assets, such as a new oven. Revenue expenditure pays for running the business in the current year, such as electricity or oven repairs.

explanation: A definition plus an example for each earns the marks.

stem: Explain why it is important to distinguish correctly between capital and revenue expenditure.

points.description: So profit is correctly stated: revenue expenditure is charged in full this year, capital expenditure only through depreciation
So non-current assets are correctly valued in the statement of financial position / users get a true and fair view

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: If they are confused, profit is wrong because expenses are overstated or understated, and the non-current assets in the statement of financial position are wrongly valued, so users are misled.

explanation: Misclassification distorts both profit and asset values (studied further in the next lesson).

stem:
Tatenda runs a building-materials business in Gweru. During the year ended 31 December 2025 he made these payments:

| Payment | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Purchase of a delivery truck | 24,900 |
| Signwriting the business name on the new truck | 360 |
| Fuel for the truck | 2,150 |
| Annual road licence | 260 |
| Air-conditioning fitted to the office for the first time | 1,850 |
| Repairs to the office door | 95 |
| Goods for resale | 31,700 |

parts.label: (a)

left.content: Signwriting the business name on the new truck
Air-conditioning fitted to the office for the first time

parts.explanation: The truck, its signwriting and the first-time air-conditioning are capital; running costs, repairs and goods for resale are revenue.

parts.label: (c)
parts.explanation: $2,150 + 260 + 95 + 31,700 = 34,205$. Goods for resale are revenue expenditure too.
parts.workedSolution: 1. $2,150 + 260 + 95 + 31,700 = 34,205$. Goods for resale are revenue expenditure too.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State where the truck and the fuel appear in Tatenda's financial statements.

points.description: Truck: non-current asset (motor vehicles at cost) in the statement of financial position
Fuel: expense in the income statement (statement of profit or loss)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The truck is a non-current asset in the statement of financial position; the fuel is an expense in the income statement.

parts.explanation: Capital → statement of financial position; revenue → income statement.

explanation: This item tests classifying expenditure and its treatment.
hints: Ask whether the spending creates or improves a long-term asset.
Goods for resale are revenue expenditure (purchases).

stem: Nyasha runs an agricultural supplies business in Chinhoyi. During the year ended 31 December 2025 her business received: commission from a seed company US\$1,260; a loan from Mutapa Finance US\$8,000; additional capital from Nyasha US\$4,500; US\$2,300 from selling an old delivery bike; and interest on a savings account US\$140. Gross profit was US\$31,450 and expenses were US\$18,925.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the total revenue receipts listed (excluding gross profit).
parts.explanation: Commission 1,260 + interest 140 = 1,400. The loan, capital and bike proceeds are capital receipts.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Commission 1,260 + interest 140 = 1,400. The loan, capital and bike proceeds are capital receipts.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare an extract from the statement of profit or loss showing the profit for the year.

points.description: Commission and interest added to gross profit (32,850)
Expenses deducted; profit for the year 13,925

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Nyasha's Agro Supplies**

**Statement of profit or loss (extract)**

**for the year ended 31 December 2025**

|  | US\$ | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Gross profit |  | 31,450 |
| Add: Commission received |  | 1,260 |
| Add: Interest received |  | 140 |
|  |  | 32,850 |
| Less: Expenses |  | (18,925) |
| **Profit for the year** |  | **13,925** |

parts.explanation: Only revenue receipts appear in the statement of profit or loss.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State where each of the three capital receipts is recorded in the statement of financial position.

points.description: Additional capital: added to capital (owner's equity)
Bike proceeds: reduce non-current assets (via the disposal of the bike)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The loan is a non-current liability; the extra capital is added to capital; the bike proceeds are part of its disposal, so the bike is removed from non-current assets.

parts.explanation: Capital receipts affect the statement of financial position, not profit.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Nyasha's assistant says the loan should be included in profit because it is money received. Evaluate this view.

points.description: The view is wrong: a loan must be repaid, so it is a liability / capital receipt, not income
Including it would overstate profit by 8,000 and could mislead Nyasha into higher drawings

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The assistant is wrong. A loan is a capital receipt that must be repaid, so it is a liability. Treating it as income would overstate profit by US\$8,000 and could lead Nyasha to take drawings the business cannot afford.

parts.explanation: Money received is not always income.

explanation: This item tests capital and revenue receipts and their treatment.
hints: Revenue receipts come from normal activities.
Capital receipts go to the statement of financial position.
